name: Hollis
positioning: Fictional over-ear headphones. In the docs it is one of three example brands: the same components in a hardware brand's colours, corners and type.
audience: People comparing premium wireless headphones on specs, battery and comfort.
voice: Specs in plain numbers: hours, grams, decibels

direction.tier: Docs example palette. It began as a hardware product page study (structure measured from Apple, Sony and Bose pages; no reference media, copy or fonts), since removed; the palette stays for the docs.
devices: Clay orange appears only on the primary action and the one accent per component
Large rounded corners, like a moulded ear cup
invariants: Black stage in dark mode, light grey in light mode
Geist for everything; numbers set large
variables: Which component the docs show in the Hollis colours

motion.character: None of its own; components keep their default motion.
motion.reducedMotion: Components follow their own reduced-motion rules.

imagery.subject: No photography: components shown in the Hollis colours
imagery.materials: Matte black plastic and aluminium, suggested by the palette only
imagery.lighting: No photography; depth from panel elevation
imagery.palette: Grey #f5f5f4, ink #1c1c1e, clay orange #c2410c on the one action
invariants: Labelled as a fictional brand wherever it appears
avoid: Reference brands' product photos, names or copy

chapters.question: How do the components look in a hardware brand?
chapters.message: The same card and controls in Hollis colours.
chapters.visual: The docs hero specimen card and every component preview when Hollis is picked.
